key_insight: SAMA factorizes instruction-guided video editing into separate semantic anchoring and motion alignment stages, enabling precise semantic changes while preserving original motion without relying on brittle external priors.
problem_solved: Existing instruction-guided video editing methods struggle to both apply accurate semantic modifications and retain faithful temporal motion; they often depend on external priors (e.g., VLM features or structural conditions) that limit robustness and generalization.
method: Semantic Anchoring: isolate and lock target semantic content to localized representations so edits are applied precisely to intended objects/regions.
Motion Alignment: preserve and align temporal dynamics by enforcing motion-consistent constraints across frames (temporal regularization/consistency mechanisms) to avoid motion collapse or artifacts.
Factorized pipeline: perform semantic editing and motion preservation as complementary, decoupled steps to reduce dependence on external priors and improve robustness.
impact: Provides a more robust, generalizable way to perform instruction-guided video edits that maintain temporal fidelity—useful for content creators and researchers aiming for high-quality, controllable video manipulation without heavy external supervision.
